newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Plot to kill Liberia's Taylor - peacekeepers.
newsitem.headline: Plot to kill Liberia's Taylor - peacekeepers.

text.p: West African peacekeepers have arrested a rival of Liberia's warlord-turned-politician Charles Taylor, saying that he has confessed to plotting to kill him in the run-up to a July 19 presidential election.

A statement from the West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG, released late on Tuesday, named the alleged plotter as Madison Wion, spokesman of the ethnic Krahn ULIMO-J faction during bloody clashes in the capital Monrovia in April and May 1996.
In a separate statement, ECOMOG chief of staff Brigadier General Abdul One Mohammed said that peacekeepers acting on a tip-off had uncovered an arms cache in a Taylor stronghold.
ECOMOG said the results of its investigation against Wion, based initially on intelligence reports, would be finalised and passed to Liberia's Justice Ministry for action.
Wion had "confessed both in writing and on tape to his involvement in the plot to kill Charles Taylor," it added.
It gave no details of the timing of the plot and made no link with an October shooting incident at the presidential palace during which Taylor was ambushed.
Two people detained with Wion about one week ago had been cleared of any involvement and had been released," it said.
Wion is managing director of Liberia's forestry authority.

General Mohammed said the arms cache, which included over 140 AK47 automatic rifles, had been found at Salala half way between Monrovia and Taylor's stronghold of Gbarnga. "We got those weapons which are capable of starting a new war as a result of a tip-off from a patriotic Liberian," he added.
Taylor and his civil war rivals Alhaji Kromah and George Boley are among 13 candidates contesting the presidential poll.

Liberia's West African neighbours rallied them around a peace deal to end the war, which Taylor launched in 1989. The conflict has killed well over 150,000 people in the republic proclaimed by freed American slaves in 1847.
